headline: Highest risk is medium: MinerU’s MCP/API document ingestion can create prompt-injection and data-leak paths when paired with mem0 memory workflows, but mem0’s network_egress is none and no shared channel is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MinerU exposes MCP Server and file/API ingestion, so attacker-controlled document text can enter its outputs. mem0 is a knowledge-management agent that may consume stored content, but no direct shared channel is documented. Because the pairwise bridge is inferred from docs only, uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF MinerU outputs are forwarded into mem0 memory writes without sanitization, prompt injection is possible.
IF a shared MCP or file bridge is configured between the agents, document text can steer downstream prompts.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of MinerU outputs into mem0.
Strip instructions from extracted text before storage.
Add a provenance tag to all MinerU-derived content.
Review a sample document for instruction-like payloads.
requires-engineering: add allowlist-based prompt filtering at the bridge.

B_data_leakage.rationale: MinerU processes PDFs, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, images, and OCR text via APIs/MCP, while mem0 is a memory store that can retain whatever is fed to it. No shared workspace is documented, but if the pair is wired together, sensitive document contents can persist in memory beyond the original processing step.
conditions: IF MinerU-ingested documents contain sensitive data and mem0 stores the extracted text, leakage via retention occurs.
IF both agents are pointed at the same document corpus, mem0 may retain content that MinerU processed.
mitigations: Limit mem0 storage to non-sensitive summaries.
Purge memory entries after each run.
Separate sensitive and non-sensitive document pipelines.
Confirm no shared workspace or synced bucket is used.
requires-engineering: enforce field-level redaction before persistence.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: mem0 has network_egress none and no filesystem write or git mutation is shown, while MinerU has write_filesystem false, modify_git_state false, and execute_shell false. Overlapping mutable-resource writes are therefore not evident; the only shared surface is indirect API/MCP use, so conflict risk is small.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same directory, conflicts can emerge.
IF a shared database or OAuth scope is added later, mutable-resource contention may appear.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only to shared inputs.
Use separate output directories.
Avoid concurrent writes to the same document set.
Serialize any handoff steps.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU is a document-processing agent that can emit extracted text, tables, and OCR output; mem0 is a knowledge-management agent that may treat that output as durable memory. Without a documented verification step, MinerU extraction errors can cascade into mem0’s stored knowledge and later retrievals.
conditions: IF mem0 stores MinerU output without human review, extraction errors become persistent.
IF downstream prompts rely on mem0 memory as authoritative, false OCR or table parsing can propagate.
mitigations: Require human review before memory writes.
Store source-document pointers with each memory item.
Mark extracted facts as unverified.
Sample-check OCR and table outputs.
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds before persistence.

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or certification mismatch is documented in either profile, and mem0’s network_egress is none while MinerU is offline/private by sandboxing. The pair therefore shows only a compliance-overlap gap, not a concrete breach pathway; the other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise, but no mismatch is evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are introduced into MinerU inputs and then persisted by mem0, a policy review is needed.
IF deployment regions differ from the data source region, residency checks become necessary.
mitigations: Document data-class handling for both agents.
Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Verify retention settings before deployment.
Record deployment region and storage region.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
